newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT - Teva buy reiterated.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Teva buy reiterated.

text.p: Lehman Brothers reiterated a 1-Buy recommendation for Teva Pharmaceutical Industries after the Israeli company received U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval for clonazepam.
The drug is a generic version of Roche's anticonvulsant Klonopin and Teva is expected to begin shipping the product within the next two weeks.

"We view the clonazepam approval as very significant, with a strong likelihood of becoming one of Teva's two largest and most profitable generic products in the United States, the other being the anti-ulcer agent sucrulfate," Lehman said in a report.

"We project potential sales in the $35 million to $45 million range (a level achievable within the next 12-18 months), translating into upwards of $0.30-$0.40 per share in aftertax earnings," the report said.
Lehman said delays in additional generic competition could boost its estimates for clonazepam.

On September 19 an FDA advisory panel is expected to release its recommendation concerning Teva's new drug application for its multiple sclerosis treatment Copaxone, which if approved would be a major boost to Teva's stock. "We continue to expect a positive recommendation from the panel, paving the way for FDA approval before year end," Lehman said.
